headline_marked: Ronaldo sends [[heartfelt support to Messi]] after death of his father
headline: Ronaldo sends heartfelt support to Messi after death of his father
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo reaches out to his long-time rival Lionel Messi following the passing of Jorge Messi, who was a central figure in the star's rise to fame.
details: Cristiano Ronaldo sent a message of support to Lionel Messi after the death of Messi's father, Jorge Messi, who passed away last week at age 68.
Ronaldo responded to Messi's emotional Instagram tribute, writing, "A huge hug to you and your loved ones during these difficult moments, Leo. Stay strong."
The gesture comes after nearly two decades of an intense individual rivalry between the two stars, highlighting the mutual respect they share beyond the football pitch.
Messi, 39, admitted he is struggling to imagine continuing his career, stating he is unsure how to move forward after the loss of his father.
Jorge Messi was a pivotal figure in his son's journey from Rosario to global stardom and served as his representative for several years.
Messi revealed that playing at the 2026 World Cup was a wish of his father's, though Argentina lost to Spain in the final after extra time.
The star also recalled breaking down in tears after scoring against Algeria, explaining he had been dealing with difficult personal circumstances.
Despite his grief, Messi vowed to raise his own children with the same influence and values that Jorge had instilled in him.
caption:
A huge hug, Leo. 🫂

Cristiano Ronaldo reaches out to Lionel Messi after the death of his father.

Cristiano Ronaldo sent a message of support to Lionel Messi after the death of Messi's father, Jorge Messi, who passed away last week at age 68.

Ronaldo responded to Messi's emotional Instagram tribute, writing, "A huge hug to you and your loved ones during these difficult moments, Leo. Stay strong."

The gesture comes after nearly two decades of an intense individual rivalry between the two stars, highlighting the mutual respect they share beyond the football pitch.

Messi, 39, admitted he is struggling to imagine continuing his career, stating he is unsure how to move forward after the loss of his father.

Jorge Messi was a pivotal figure in his son's journey from Rosario to global stardom and served as his representative for several years.

Messi revealed that playing at the 2026 World Cup was a wish of his father's, though Argentina lost to Spain in the final after extra time.

The star also recalled breaking down in tears after scoring against Algeria, explaining he had been dealing with difficult personal circumstances.

Despite his grief, Messi vowed to raise his own children with the same influence and values that Jorge had instilled in him.

headline: Power crisis: Shops and malls must close by 8pm nationwide
summary: The government has tightened electricity conservation measures, directing all markets to shut earlier and billboards to be switched off by 7pm.
details: Shopping malls, markets, and shops across Bangladesh must now close by 8:00pm as the government intensifies efforts to conserve electricity during the ongoing power crisis.
According to a directive from the Power Division, businesses are permitted to operate from 11:00am to 8:00pm, moving up the previous closing time of 9:00pm.
The new rules also mandate that all lit billboards be switched off by 7:00pm, and all decorative lighting must remain off at all times.
These restrictions extend to all ongoing and upcoming fairs and cultural programs across the country, which are now required to end by 8:00pm.
However, essential services including hospitals, pharmacies, and restaurants are exempt from these new closing time restrictions.
caption:
Shopping malls and markets nationwide must now shut by 8pm. The government is tightening power-saving measures to combat the electricity crisis.

Shopping malls, markets, and shops across Bangladesh must now close by 8:00pm as the government intensifies efforts to conserve electricity during the ongoing power crisis.

According to a directive from the Power Division, businesses are permitted to operate from 11:00am to 8:00pm, moving up the previous closing time of 9:00pm.

The new rules also mandate that all lit billboards be switched off by 7:00pm, and all decorative lighting must remain off at all times.

These restrictions extend to all ongoing and upcoming fairs and cultural programs across the country, which are now required to end by 8:00pm.

However, essential services including hospitals, pharmacies, and restaurants are exempt from these new closing time restrictions.
